thread:
eli_customer: Hey, we're seeing a sustained wave of 429s from the API for the last ~40m. Impacting ingestion pipeline and UI features. Sample request IDs from our logs: r-176340-0a1b2c, r-176340-0a1b2d, r-176340-0a1b3e. Happened across two client hosts 10.4.1.22 and 10.4.1.23.

maria_support: Sorry about the trouble — can you paste one full response header + the exact curl you ran? Also upload a HAR if you have it. Quick checks: is this the hosted API key or dedicated instance?

eli_customer: Hosted API (api.redwood.example). Here's one response we copied straight from the client: 

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:17:03 GMT
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
content-length: 86
retry-after: 2
x-request-id: r-176340-0a1b2c
x-rate-limit-limit: 300
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1763401805

And the curl we used to repro (redacted key):

curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3-small","input":"test"}'

jon_eng: Thanks. Two quick observations: x-rate-limit-limit 300 suggests a per-minute window. remaining 0 + short Retry-After 2 implies burst consumed tokens. Can you check whether you have multiple processes reusing the same API key? Also, did the client start a new job around 14:15?

eli_customer: We did a deployment at 14:14 that spun up 10 workers that all start a catch-up job. Might be correlated. Uploading a HAR and our debug bundle now (link): https://files.redwood.example/debug/eli/176340/debug-bundle-176340.tar.gz

maria_support: Got the bundle. Can you also capture a short tcpdump or packet count? We want to see the request timestamps granularity. If you can run: 

# run on one of the hosts for 30s during repro
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host api.redwood.example and port 443 -w /tmp/capture.pcap

jon_eng: Also please try a controlled curl loop to reproduce the burst pattern while we tail access logs. Example script to simulate 10 workers each sending 5 req/s: 

for i in $(seq 1 10); do \
  (for j in $(seq 1 50); do \
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total} %{size_download}\n" -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-3-small","input":"ping"}' &\
    sleep 0.2\
  done) &\
 done
 wait

alex_sre: I'm tailing ingress logs now. Seeing lots of requests from the same API key at ~120 rps starting 14:15:05 UTC. Sample from proxy logs: 

[2026-03-10T14:15:07.123Z] x-request-id=r-176340-0a1b2c api_key=acct_ABC123 client_ip=10.4.1.22 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=429 rt=0.045
[2026-03-10T14:15:07.130Z] x-request-id=r-176340-0a1b2d api_key=acct_ABC123 client_ip=10.4.1.22 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=429 rt=0.043
[2026-03-10T14:15:07.135Z] x-request-id=r-176340-0a1b3e api_key=acct_ABC123 client_ip=10.4.1.23 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=429 rt=0.047

alex_sre: In the same minute earlier we had these counters for the key acct_ABC123: total_requests=720, allowed=300, denied=420. That maps to the x-rate-limit-limit header. Looks like client bursted past the per-minute quota.

maria_support: That matches. Two paths forward: (1) If you can change the client to add jitter/throttle to keep sustained rps under the quota OR (2) request a quota increase / switch to dedicated. For immediate relief, we can issue a short-term token with a higher rate but that requires auth approval.

eli_customer: We want to avoid changing infra tonight if possible. Can you issue a temporary token? Also want to understand whether retries are exacerbating the burst (client has exponential backoff but initial spikes with 10 workers are overlapping).

jon_eng: Before issuing token, can you confirm retries? From the HAR I see the client is retrying on timeouts with no backoff for first 3 attempts. Sample snippet: 

{"timestamp":"2026-03-10T14:15:08Z","event":"retry","request_id":"r-176340-0a1b2e","status":"timeout","attempt":2}

jon_eng: If retries fire immediately across workers that amplifies burst by N. Suggest patching client to stagger start and add random initial delay (0-500ms) and exponential backoff starting at 500ms.

maria_support: For our diagnostics: I attached a minimal trace file from the ingress (s3://redwood-internal/traces/176340/trace-176340.json) and flagged the key. If you want a temporary token I can start the approvals; I'll need the account owner email and intended duration.

eli_customer: Owner is ops+eli@custco.example. We need temp token for 2 hours. Please start approval. In parallel we'll deploy a quick fix to add jitter and reduce worker spin-up concurrency.

alex_sre: Noted. Also captured token-scoped counters: 

acct_ABC123 window_start=2026-03-10T14:15:00Z window_end=2026-03-10T14:16:00Z requests=720 accepted=300 throttled=420
acct_ABC123 window_start=2026-03-10T14:16:00Z window_end=2026-03-10T14:17:00Z requests=310 accepted=300 throttled=10

maria_support: Approval flow kicked off. Next steps for you: upload tcpdump, confirm you applied jitter patch, and paste any additional request IDs if you see new 429s after we issue token. We'll follow up once approval completes (ETA ~20m). :thumbsup:

eli_customer: Uploading tcpdump now. Thanks all, will report back after patch/deploy.

deploy-bot: Deploy started by eli (branch/ops/throttle-fix) at 2026-03-10T14:30:10Z — status: in_progress

eli_customer: Deploy finished and initial smoke shows 200s with reduced rps. Will monitor. If we still see intermittent 429s we'll reopen.

maria_support: Closing this thread for now — we'll keep the temp token approval pending until ops confirms. If anything changes ping here and we'll reopen.
